levels.tagline: The basics every spreadsheet needs. Learn these before anything else.

formulas.name: SUM
formulas.what: Adds all numbers in a range.
formulas.tip: Add a bowler's total wickets across all matches.

formulas.name: AVERAGE
formulas.what: Returns the mean of all numbers in a range.
formulas.tip: Find a batsman's average runs per innings.

formulas.name: MIN
formulas.what: Returns the smallest number in a range.
formulas.tip: Find the best (lowest) economy rate in the squad.

formulas.name: MAX
formulas.what: Returns the largest number in a range.
formulas.tip: Find the highest score in a tournament.

formulas.name: COUNT
formulas.what: Counts cells that contain numbers.
formulas.tip: Count how many innings have been recorded.

formulas.name: COUNTA
formulas.what: Counts cells that are not empty (numbers or text).
formulas.tip: Count how many player names are listed.

formulas.name: ROUND
formulas.what: Rounds a number to a given number of decimal places.
formulas.tip: Round a batting average to two decimal places.

formulas.name: ABS
formulas.what: Returns the absolute value (removes the minus sign).
formulas.tip: Find the run difference between two teams regardless of sign.

formulas.name: Cell reference
formulas.what: Points to a single cell. Use it inside formulas to refer to a value.
formulas.tip: Add two individual scores together.

formulas.name: Range reference
formulas.what: Points to a block of cells. Most functions accept a range.
formulas.tip: Refer to a whole column of run scores at once.

levels.tagline: Make decisions with IF, count and sum with conditions, and lock references.

formulas.name: IF
formulas.what: Returns one value when a condition is true, another when false.
formulas.tip: Flag players who scored 30 or more as 'Good'.

formulas.name: IFS
formulas.what: Tests multiple conditions in order and returns the first matching value.
formulas.tip: Grade batsmen into tiers based on their score.

formulas.name: AND
formulas.what: Returns TRUE only when all conditions are true.
formulas.tip: Find an all-rounder: scored 30 AND took 2 wickets.

formulas.name: OR
formulas.what: Returns TRUE when at least one condition is true.
formulas.tip: Flag a standout match: 50 runs OR 5 wickets.

formulas.name: COUNTIF
formulas.what: Counts cells that match a single condition.
formulas.tip: Count how many times Ujwal appears in the squad list.

formulas.name: COUNTIFS
formulas.what: Counts rows where multiple conditions are all true.
formulas.tip: Count Ujwal's innings where he took more than one wicket.

formulas.name: SUMIF
formulas.what: Adds values in sum_range only where range matches the criteria.
formulas.tip: Total all runs scored by Ujwal.

formulas.name: SUMIFS
formulas.what: Adds values where multiple conditions are all true.
formulas.tip: Total Ujwal's runs in matches where he also took wickets.

formulas.name: AVERAGEIF
formulas.what: Averages values in average_range only where range matches.
formulas.tip: Find Ujwal's batting average across all his innings.

formulas.name: Absolute reference
formulas.what: The $ sign locks a row or column so the reference does not shift when you copy the formula.
formulas.tip: Divide each player's runs by the team total in a fixed cell.

levels.tagline: Find data in tables, clean messy text, and use statistical rankings.

formulas.name: VLOOKUP
formulas.what: Searches the first column of a table and returns a value from another column in the same row.
formulas.tip: Look up a player name and return their batting average. Use FALSE for exact match.

formulas.name: XLOOKUP
formulas.what: Modern lookup that searches any range and returns a value from a separate return range.
formulas.tip: More flexible than VLOOKUP: the lookup and return columns can be anywhere.

formulas.name: MATCH
formulas.what: Returns the position (1-based) of a value inside a range. Use 0 for exact match.
formulas.tip: Find what row number Rohan is on in the squad list.

formulas.name: INDEX
formulas.what: Returns the value at a specific row and column position inside a range.
formulas.tip: Return the 3rd value in the runs column.

formulas.name: INDEX + MATCH
formulas.what: Combines INDEX and MATCH to look up a value in any direction.
formulas.tip: The go-to flexible lookup. MATCH finds the row, INDEX returns the value.

formulas.name: TRIM
formulas.what: Removes leading, trailing, and extra internal spaces from text.
formulas.tip: Clean player names that have accidental spaces before or after them.

formulas.name: UPPER
formulas.what: Converts all letters in a text string to upper case.
formulas.tip: Standardise team names to all capitals for consistency.

formulas.name: LOWER
formulas.what: Converts all letters to lower case.
formulas.tip: Normalise email addresses or codes before comparing them.

formulas.name: LEN
formulas.what: Returns the number of characters in a text string.
formulas.tip: Check if a player's jersey number code is exactly 3 characters.

formulas.name: LEFT
formulas.what: Returns the first N characters from the left of a string.
formulas.tip: Extract the three-letter country code from a player ID.

formulas.name: RIGHT
formulas.what: Returns the last N characters from the right of a string.
formulas.tip: Extract the two-digit number at the end of a match code.

formulas.name: MID
formulas.what: Returns N characters starting from a given position.
formulas.tip: Pull the zone code out of the middle of a stadium identifier string.

formulas.name: MEDIAN
formulas.what: Returns the middle value when the range is sorted. Less affected by extreme scores than AVERAGE.
formulas.tip: Find the typical score in a series without big centuries skewing the number.

formulas.name: LARGE
formulas.what: Returns the k-th largest value in a range.
formulas.tip: Find the second-highest score in a match.

formulas.name: SMALL
formulas.what: Returns the k-th smallest value in a range.
formulas.tip: Find the best (lowest) economy rate in the squad.

levels.tagline: Multiply arrays, count unique items, and work across multiple data dimensions.

formulas.name: SUMPRODUCT
formulas.what: Multiplies matching elements across arrays and sums all the products.
formulas.tip: Multiply overs by economy rate for each bowler, then sum to get total runs conceded.

formulas.name: COUNTUNIQUE
formulas.what: Returns the number of distinct non-empty values in a range.
formulas.tip: Count how many different venues have hosted matches this season.

levels.tagline: Dynamic array functions that return whole ranges of results at once.

formulas.name: FILTER
formulas.what: Returns only the rows from a range that match a condition.
formulas.tip: Return all players who scored more than 50. Google Sheets only.

formulas.name: UNIQUE
formulas.what: Returns one copy of each distinct row in a range.
formulas.tip: Get a deduplicated list of venues from the match log. Google Sheets only.

formulas.name: SORT
formulas.what: Returns a sorted copy of a range without changing the original data.
formulas.tip: Sort the squad by runs in descending order. Google Sheets only.

levels.tagline: Build reusable formula building blocks and model complex scenarios.

formulas.name: LET
formulas.what: Assigns a name to a value inside a formula so you can reuse it without repeating it.
formulas.tip: Name the squad average once and use it throughout a complex formula.

formulas.name: LAMBDA
formulas.what: Creates a reusable custom function. Assign it to a named range to call it like any built-in function.
formulas.tip: Build your own economy-rate formula and reuse it across the whole sheet.
